title: Guidelines on Management of Climate Related and Environmental Financial Risks in Banks and Bank Holding Companies (Reserve Bank of Malawi, October 2024)
citation: Reserve Bank of Malawi, Bank Supervision Department, Guidelines on Management of Climate Related and Environmental Financial Risks in Banks and Bank Holding Companies, October 2024, issued under s. 96 of the Financial Services Act, 2010
evidence: The cover of the PDF reads "OCTOBER, 2024"; paragraph 2.1: "These Guidelines are issued pursuant to Section 96 of the Financial Services Act, 2010." The PDF has no commencement clause and no day. The Bank's Directives for Banks page lists it as "Guidelines on Management of Climate Related Financial Risks for Banks and Bank Holding Companies 2024" with the date "Apr 15, 2025" (the date of the web upload). Opened 2026-11-05: curl with a browser User-Agent, 200 268929 application/octet-stream, 14 pages, sha256 c3e24e5f1d1d56f0742e1bab3b1484277e40ac38609097660cd7975d50501223.
notes: Link only: row MW-RBM-ADOPTED is permission requested (the Bank's site footer reads 'Copyright 2026 Reserve Bank of Malawi. All Rights Reserved.', no terms page exists, and Copyright Act 2016 s. 28(1)(a) is not shown to cover a supervisory guideline). The text is mainly a prudential risk-management directive (Parts I and II: board oversight, risk management process, scenario analysis and stress testing, F6 content), but Part III sets a public disclosure duty, so the family is F1: paragraph 10.1 "A bank and bank holding company shall disclose, at least on an annual basis, in its annual reports, information on climate related and environmental financial risks it is exposed to, the potential impact of material risks and its approach to manage these risks." Paragraph 3.1(c) frames the disclosure principles as ones banks 'may use'. Whether the Guidelines bind is not stated: the file name served by the Bank is '... final draft.pdf', the title says Guidelines, the operative paragraphs say 'shall', and the register row keeps binding unknown. in_force is null because only the month (October 2024) is printed. The earlier register row said the PDF could not be opened; it opens with curl and a browser User-Agent.
status_note: Permission request to the Reserve Bank of Malawi not sent.

title: Malawi Stock Exchange Listings Requirements (revised April 2023), rule 7.42 Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Reporting
citation: Malawi Stock Exchange, Listings Requirements, revised in April 2023, Part C Section 7 (Continuing Obligation), rule 7.42
evidence: The cover reads "REVISED IN APRIL 2023" on every page; rule 7.42(1): "The issuer shall be required to disclose the relevance of sustainability in the context of environmental, social and governance standards to the company and the company's strategy for addressing sustainability issues." Rule 7.42(4): "The issuer shall provide sustainability information either- (a) in an annual report ... (c) a standalone sustainability report". The document gives no commencement day. Opened 2026-11-05 from https://mse.co.mw/upload/22: curl with a browser User-Agent, 200 2458773 application/octet-stream, 260 pages, sha256 dc69d1191bdfe17a9114317d0dd79427fc8d20c576bb8bb1f88c55cc81c85f37.
notes: Link only: row MW-MSE-ADOPTED is permission requested (MSE disclaimer: copyright of the Malawi Stock Exchange, personal and non-commercial use only). A binding listing rule: Section 1 states the Rules and the Board's interpretation 'are conclusive and binding on an issuer'. The rule requires listed issuers to disclose sustainability policy, risk mitigation and performance data (7.42(2)(a)) in the annual report or a standalone report; 7.42(3)(b) says the issuer 'shall apply the latest versions of GRI Guidelines or Standards to the level applicable to its context' while (2)(c) says issuers are 'encouraged to apply' GRI; assurance is not mandatory (7.42(5)). This is the April 2023 text; press reports of 2025 (Nation Online, 2025-07-03) that revised rules require ESG disclosure from the 2024 financial year were not matched to a later revision: the MSE page lists only this one Listings Requirements file. in_force is null because only the revision month is printed.
status_note: Permission request to the Malawi Stock Exchange not sent.

title: Malawi Stock Exchange Guidelines for Issuance of Sustainable Bonds (June 2023, Version 1.0)
citation: Malawi Stock Exchange, Guidelines for Issuance of Sustainable Bonds, Version 1.0, June 2023
evidence: The cover reads "June 2023 Version 1.0"; paragraph 1.1: "These rules shall apply to sustainable bonds including green, social, gender bonds and any other sustainable-themed bond acceptable to the Exchange." No commencement day is printed. Opened 2026-11-05 from https://mse.co.mw/upload/25: curl with a browser User-Agent, 200 160601 application/octet-stream, sha256 d570ad8eeb3d0337d0f265c67ed87f8ee7025a3426428afe5942763e5bacb251.
notes: Link only: row MW-MSE-ADOPTED is permission requested. The rules govern listing of sustainable-labelled bonds: an Independent Verifier's pre-issuance review (2.2), a sustainable bond framework (2.1), use-of-proceeds, escrow and reporting duties (2.5, 5.0) and non-compliance provisions (6.0). They are issuer-side labelling and verification rules, so F6, not a corporate disclosure rule. in_force is null because only the month is printed.
status_note: Permission request to the Malawi Stock Exchange not sent.

title: Environment Management Act, 2016 (Act No. 19 of 2017)
citation: Environment Management Act, 2016 (Act No. 19 of 2017), Malawi Gazette Supplement 5C of 5 May 2017; assented to 30 April 2017
evidence: Laws.Africa Commons page of the Act (a reproduction of the Gazette, not an official host), opened 2026-11-05: "Published in Malawi Gazette Supplement 5C on 5 May 2017 / Assented to on 30 April 2017 / Commenced on 1 November 2019 by Environment Management Act, 2016: Commencement" (https://commons.laws.africa/akn/mw/act/2017/19/eng@2017-05-05.pdf, 200 145335 application/pdf). No official page was reachable. The commencing notice itself was not read.
notes: Link only: row MW-MALAWILII-ADOPTED is permission requested (MalawiLII terms: CC BY-NC 4.0, scraping prohibited; document pages answer curl with a Cloudflare 403). The Gazette supplement scan at https://commons.laws.africa/akn/mw/act/2017/19/media/publication/mw-act-2017-19-publication-document.pdf (200 4393078 application/pdf, text layer present, sha256 a3cffb85271502df1dc4abf7f7ac7102202e4955f5e010f2111fe389794e35c0) is a state publication hosted by a private party; whether it counts as the state-published text under Copyright Act 2016 s. 28(1)(a) is Varun's call and nothing was stored. The text of the scan has section 54 'Control and management of factors affecting climate change' and defines 'climate change'; the framework act, no stand-alone climate act was found. The brief's note that Government Notice No. 73 of 2019 calls it the 'Environment Management Act, 2016' matches the Commons title. No state host serves it: the Government of Malawi site's Acts page (https://www.malawi.gov.mw/index.php/resources/publications/acts, 200) lists six downloads, none of them this Act, and no copy of the commencement notice was found online at a state host.
status_note: Permission request to MalawiLII not sent.

title: Consumer Protection Act (Cap. 48:10; Act No. 14 of 2003)
citation: Consumer Protection Act, 2003 (Cap. 48:10), assented to 13 November 2003
evidence: Laws.Africa Commons PDF as at 31 December 2014 (a reproduction, not an official host), opened 2026-11-05: "Chapter 48:10 / Assented to on 13 November 2003 / Commenced on 21 October 2004" (https://commons.laws.africa/akn/mw/act/2003/14/eng@2014-12-31.pdf, 200 356426 application/pdf).
notes: Link only: row MW-MALAWILII-CONSOLIDATED is permission requested. Provisions read on the reproduction: s. 2 defines 'false or misleading advertising' and 'abusive advertising' (which 'infringes environmental values'); s. 44(1)(a) advertisement must conform to 'decency, sincerity and truth', s. 44(2) a false or misleading offer or promotion 'shall be guilty of fraud'; s. 2 'unfair trade practice' includes false representations of standard, quality or grade; a supplier's duty not to engage in unfair trade practices sits in the list of supplier duties ('not engage in any unfair trade practices'). No environmental-claims rule as such. The Commons PDF footer says 'Licensed under CC-BY', the Commons page says CC-BY-NC-SA; neither is used. The Competition and Fair Trading Commission administers the Act with the Competition and Fair Trading Act.
status_note: Permission request to MalawiLII not sent.

title: Competition and Fair Trading Act (Cap. 48:09; Act No. 43 of 1998)
citation: Competition and Fair Trading Act, 1998 (Cap. 48:09), s. 43 Unfair trading
evidence: Laws.Africa Commons PDF as at 31 December 2014 (a reproduction, not an official host), opened 2026-11-05: "Chapter 48:09 / Commenced on 1 April 2000" (https://commons.laws.africa/akn/mw/act/1998/43/eng@2014-12-31.pdf, 200 319898 application/pdf).
notes: Link only: row MW-MALAWILII-CONSOLIDATED is permission requested. Section 43(1)(k): a person shall not, in relation to a consumer, "put out an advertisement which is misleading or deceptive"; s. 43(2): contravention is an offence. The version read is the 2014 consolidation. MalawiLII also lists a Competition and Fair Trading Act, 2024 (Act No. 20 of 2024, https://malawilii.org/akn/mw/act/2024/20/eng@2024-05-31); the Commons PDF of it is a stub and says 'Note: This Act has not yet come into force' as at 31 May 2024, and MalawiLII lists Competition and Fair Trading Regulations, 2026 (GN 27 of 2026), so commencement and repeal of the 1998 Act are not established: which text is current was not confirmed.
status_note: Permission request to MalawiLII not sent.
